readout_other: Antisaccade/prosaccade task: saccade latency, error rate, amplitude, peak velocity and skewness measured via infrared eye tracking
direction_notes: Ipsilateral antisaccade latencies were significantly slowed by FUS to the left FEF (monkey Y and L), with a marginal increase in contralateral error rate for one monkey; no significant effect on contralateral latencies, saccade amplitude, peak velocity or skewness, and no effect when the transducer was aimed at premotor cortex or in sham (transducer moved away) sessions.
safety_notes: All acoustic parameters (MI, ISPPA, ISPTA) were far below FDA diagnostic ultrasound imaging safety limits, and no discomfort was imposed on the animals during ultrasonic neurostimulation.

exposures.label: FUS to the left frontal eye field during antisaccade task

timing.protocol_description: FUS pulses were delivered to the left FEF at a 100 ms stimulus onset asynchrony after visual target appearance, with rise and fall times of 1 ms, and a minimum 30 s pause between each ultrasonic pulse. Each session comprised a 100-trial AS baseline block, a 400-trial block (360 without FUS, 40 with FUS pseudorandomly interleaved, 20 per side), and a 100-trial posttest block.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Two macaques (Macaca mulatta ‘‘Y’’ and ‘‘L’’) participated in this study.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Monkey Y performed ten sessions and monkey L twelve sessions.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The frequency was set to 320 kHz and the pulse duration to 100 ms using a first function generator, with rise and fall times set to 1 ms using a second generator (AFG3101, Tektronix) connected to the amplitude modulation entry of the first one.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The frequency was set to 320 kHz and the pulse duration to 100 ms using a first function generator, with rise and fall times set to 1 ms using a second generator (AFG3101, Tektronix) connected to the amplitude modulation entry of the first one.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: The pressure amplitude at focus was set to 0.6 MPa, as measured in free water with a heterodyne interferometer.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: 0.35 MPa in the brain of the monkeys. The corresponding mechanical index (MI) is 0.6 6 0.1 W/cm<sup>2</sup> and intensity spatial peak pulse average (ISPPA) is $4 \pm 1 . 1 ~ \mathsf { W } / \mathsf { c m } ^ { 2 }$ behind the skull.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.isppa_w_cm2: 0.35 MPa in the brain of the monkeys. The corresponding mechanical index (MI) is 0.6 6 0.1 W/cm<sup>2</sup> and intensity spatial peak pulse average (ISPPA) is $4 \pm 1 . 1 ~ \mathsf { W } / \mathsf { c m } ^ { 2 }$ behind the skull.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.ispta_w_cm2: By taking into account a minimum 30 s pause between each ultrasonic pulse, we also estimated the corresponding spatial peak time average intensity (ISPTA) at less than 13.5 6 3.8 mW/cm<sup>2</sup>.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: A single-element ultrasound transducer (H115, diameter 64 mm, Sonic Concept), geometrically focused to 63 mm, was used with a coupling cone (C103, Sonic Concepts) filled with degassed water.
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: A single-element ultrasound transducer (H115, diameter 64 mm, Sonic Concept), geometrically focused to 63 mm, was used with a coupling cone (C103, Sonic Concepts) filled with degassed water.

flags.reason: The 0.35 MPa in-brain value, ISPPA and ISPTA are derated estimates based on skull-transmission measurements at seven locations on an ex vivo macaque skull specimen (mean ± SD), not measurements in the live animals; reported_as coded as mean_or_range_across_subjects for lack of a closer category.
Paper reports ISPTA as an upper bound ('at less than 13.5 ± 3.8 mW/cm2'); the stated value is recorded as-is rather than as a strict mean.
Two distinct control manipulations were used: stimulation of a control site (premotor cortex) and a sham condition where the transducer was moved 4 cm away; both are listed.
